name: Oneiravex
description: Oneiravex is an SNT-compatible neuromodulator that amplifies hippocampal and visual cortex activity during REM sleep, producing hyper-saturated, narratively coherent dreams with full sensory fidelity. Dreams experienced under Oneiravex are frequently reported as more emotionally real than waking life, with colors, textures, and interpersonal dynamics that exceed conscious perception.
effects: Enhanced emotional depth and narrative coherence in dreams
side_effects: Waking reality dysphoria — real life feels muted and unsatisfying
Escalating dose requirements for same effect
Rare: persistent visual bleed-through (dream imagery overlaid on waking vision)
cultural_context: Oneiravex has spawned an entire subculture of 'dream artists' in Tier 3-4 who share and discuss their chemically enhanced dream experiences like reviewing films. Some use it recreationally before sleep to experience a second life. Therapists use it in controlled settings for grief processing. the Gray Zone sees bootleg versions called 'Vivids' that are inconsistently dosed and occasionally catastrophic.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 dream artist has been sharing their Oneiravex dreams publicly — but the dreams contain accurate details about a Lazarus Pharmaceuticals black site that the dreamer has never visited.
Helix Biosystems is quietly tracking what users dream about through a buried SNT telemetry function in the drug's metabolite pathway — and selling the aggregate emotional data to media corporations.

Someone in the Gray Zone is synthesizing a Vivids variant that doesn't just enhance dreams — it lets two people on the same batch share the same dreamscape. The implications are terrifying and beautiful in equal measure.
